claim: The English "How will you go?" fits どうやっていきますか as well as なんでいきますか, and the deck itself says the two are interchangeable.
evidence: Production front: "Transport / How will you go?" with no hint. chapter-7-extras/how note: "Interchangeable with なんで (nande) from this lesson for asking how someone travels; どうやって (dō yatte) is the everyday choice".
fix: Add a hint naming the word wanted, e.g. "use なんで (nande)", or a scene that rules out どうやって.

claim: The front "What day" most naturally asks for a weekday in English, which is the answer of chapter-7/nanyoubi, not なんにち.
evidence: Production front: "Time / What day". chapter-7/nanyoubi Production front: "Time / What day of the week" (answer なんようび). The date cards all say "(of the month)".
fix: Gloss it "What day (of the month)" or "What date", matching the date cards.

claim: The note says dates from the 11th onward are regular, but this same chapter teaches the 14th, 20th and 24th as irregular.
evidence: Note: "Days 1st–10th of the month have irregular readings that must be memorized individually; from the 11th onward the pattern becomes regular: number + にち". chapter-7/juuyokka-14th note: "Irregular — built from よっか"; hatsuka-20th note: "Irregular reading — not にじゅうにち"; nijuuyokka-24th note: "Irregular".
fix: Say the 1st to 10th, the 14th, the 20th and the 24th are irregular, and the rest are number + にち.

claim: The note says にち names every day of the month from the 11th onward, which would make the 14th じゅうよんにち and the 20th にじゅうにち; it also says the chapter spells days in hiragana while this chapter's own cards use numerals.
evidence: Note: "attaches after a number to name a day of the month (from the 11th onward) ... This chapter spells days out in hiragana". Same chapter: juuyokka-14th じゅうよっか, hatsuka-20th はつか; 12nichi-ni front "12にちに"; fib-ryokou-4-29-5-5-a front "4がつ29にちから5がついつかまでです".
fix: Add "except the 14th, 20th and 24th" and drop the sentence about how this chapter spells days.

claim: The note says this chapter spells months in hiragana, but cards in this chapter write months with numerals, so the note describes something the learner does not see.
evidence: Note: "This chapter spells months out in hiragana, but elsewhere in the book they're written with numerals, e.g. 1がつ". Same chapter: ks1-emma-april front "エマさんは４がつににほんにきました"; fib-ryokou-4-29-5-5-a front "4がつ29にちから5がついつかまでです".
fix: Drop the remark about this chapter's spelling and just say months are often written with numerals, e.g. 4がつ for しがつ.

claim: The Recognition hint describes the answer ("a longer stretch away from work") so the front reads as a definition of "vacation".
evidence: Recognition front: "やすみ / a longer stretch away from work"; back: "Answer: Vacation, day off". The learner already knows やすみ as "Break, time off" (chapter-3).
fix: Make the Recognition hint a context rather than a definition, e.g. "as in なつやすみ".

claim: The note names a "まし past-tense pattern", but the past ending the learner was taught is ました, not まし.
evidence: Note: "The まし past-tense pattern from いきました／きました extends to かえります too."
fix: Say "the ました (mashita) past from いきました／きました works for かえります too: かえりました."

claim: The English "How is Smith-san going to Osaka?" fits both なんで and どうやって, and the deck tells the learner どうやって is the everyday choice.
evidence: Production front: "Transport / How is Smith-san going to Osaka?" with no hint. chapter-7-extras/how note: "Interchangeable with なんで (nande) from this lesson for asking how someone travels; どうやって (dō yatte) is the everyday choice".
fix: Add a hint naming なんで (nande), as the に/へ pair in this unit does for its particle.

claim: The English "How is Tanaka-san going to the meeting?" fits both なんで and どうやって, with nothing on the front to choose.
evidence: Production front: "Transport / How is Tanaka-san going to the meeting?" with no hint. chapter-7-extras/how note: "Interchangeable with なんで (nande) from this lesson for asking how someone travels; どうやって (dō yatte) is the everyday choice".
fix: Add a hint naming なんで (nande).

claim: The English "How does Kato-san come to the office?" fits both なんで and どうやって, with nothing on the front to choose.
evidence: Production front: "Transport / How does Kato-san come to the office?" with no hint. chapter-7-extras/how note: "Interchangeable with なんで (nande) from this lesson for asking how someone travels; どうやって (dō yatte) is the everyday choice".
fix: Add a hint naming なんで (nande).

claim: The English "How do you get to the gym?" fits なんでジムにいきますか as well as どうやって, the form every なんで card in this chapter drills.
evidence: Production front: "Transport / How do you get to the gym?" with no hint. chapter-7/nande-ikimasuka note: "なにで (nani de) can be used instead when asking about means of transportation"; chapter-7/nande-ikimasuka "How will you go?" = なんでいきますか.
fix: Add a hint naming どうやって (dō yatte).

claim: The English "How do you go to work?" fits なんでしごとにいきますか as well as どうやって, with nothing on the front to choose.
evidence: Production front: "Transport / How do you go to work?" with no hint. chapter-7-extras/fib-tanaka-nande-kaigi-q "How is Tanaka-san going to the meeting?" = なんで....
fix: Add a hint naming どうやって (dō yatte).

claim: The hint glosses the destination に as "in/on/at", which is the gloss of the time に this chapter teaches as a different job.
evidence: Production front hint: "use the に (ni, "in/on/at") destination particle". chapter-6 に: "To (particle, indicates direction of movement)"; chapter-7/ni-particle-time: "At, in, on (particle) / marking a point in time".
fix: Gloss it as "use the に (ni, "to") destination particle".

claim: The note says きません appears on no other card, but the learner studied a きません card and two きません sentences in Lesson 6 extras.
evidence: Note: "きません (kimasen) appears on no other card, though its partner いきません (ikimasen) does." Ledger, chapter-6-extras: "きません | Do not come, will not come", "チャンさんはあしたとうきょうししゃにきません", "いいえ、きません".
fix: Delete the second sentence, or point back to Lesson 6's きません instead.

claim: The note calls this "Member 1 of a ... set", which means nothing on a shuffled card met alone.
evidence: Note: "Member 1 of a かえります (kaerimasu) / かえりません (kaerimasen) / かえりますか (kaerimasu ka) set on the same sentence."
fix: Drop the "Member 1" wording; keep the に point.

claim: The note opens "Member 2 of the set", which points at sibling cards the learner is not looking at.
evidence: Note: "Member 2 of the set: ます (masu) becomes ません (masen) and nothing else in the sentence moves."
fix: Drop "Member 2 of the set:" and keep the rest.

claim: The note opens "Member 3 of the set", which points at sibling cards the learner is not looking at.
evidence: Note: "Member 3 of the set: か (ka) is simply added to the end, with no change to word order."
fix: Drop "Member 3 of the set:" and keep the rest.

claim: The note ends with "Member 1 of a ... set", which means nothing on a shuffled card met alone.
evidence: Note: "... Member 1 of a きます (kimasu) / きません (kimasen) / きますか (kimasu ka) set."
fix: Drop the "Member 1" sentence; keep the two-に explanation.

claim: The note opens "Member 2 of the set", which points at sibling cards the learner is not looking at.
evidence: Note: "Member 2 of the set. きません (kimasen) appears on no other card, ..."
fix: Drop "Member 2 of the set."

claim: The note refers to "the set" and to "the いつ question the exercises drill", neither of which the learner has in front of them.
evidence: Note: "Member 3 of the set — a yes/no question, unlike the いつ (itsu) question the exercises drill."
fix: Replace with something the card itself shows, e.g. "A yes/no question: add か (ka) to the statement."

claim: This card has exactly the same target as a Lesson 6 extras card, so the learner studies the same sentence twice under two almost identical fronts.
evidence: This card: "3ばんのバスがいきます", front "The No. 3 bus goes there. / answering which bus goes to the airport". chapter-6-extras/fib-sanban-no-basu-ikimasu: "3ばんのバスがいきます", front "The No. 3 bus goes. / answering which bus goes to Shibuya".
fix: Change the number (or the sentence) on this card, or drop it as already taught.

claim: The English "I'll go there next Monday." loses the "where you are" sense of そちら, so the learner cannot tell that そちら is wanted rather than あちら.
evidence: Production front: "Travel & Tourism / I'll go there next Monday." Ledger, chapter-6-extras: "あしたそちらにいきます | I will go there (where you are) tomorrow."; chapter-5 あちら "Over there (away from both of us)".
fix: Gloss it "I'll go there (where you are) next Monday.", as the Lesson 6 card does.

claim: The scene asks what time you will come, but the answer uses いきます (go), and nothing on the card says why going, not coming, is the right reply.
evidence: Production front: "I'll go at 10:00. / answering what time you'll come"; answer "10じにいきます". No note.
fix: Add a note: when someone asks "will you come?", you answer with いきます because you are going to where they are.
